scope: Theorem 1.1 (Refined recovery) of the manuscript “Single-exponential recovery and bounded-price strictness for metric k-median” (preprints/Single-Exponential-Recovery-and-Bounded-Price-Strictness-for-Metric-k-Median-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 125 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 823fdb284a7d3c0e), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 2. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let D and F be disjoint indexed sets in a metric whose distances between distinct indices are positive integers bounded by a fixed polynomial in N = |D| + |F|. Fix ε > 0 and 0 < L0 < ∞, and choose a fixed rational parameter 0 < µ ≤ min{1/4, ε/12}. Let S ⊆ F have cardinality h ≥ 1. Suppose there exists a comparison solution O ⊆ F of cardinality h and cost P > 0, with a partition into good and bad centers and distinct proxies ϕi ∈ S for the good centers, such that X i good X p∈Ci d(p, ϕi) ≤ Pg + µP, m := |{i : i bad}| ≤ L0 log N. (1.1) Given S, µ, L0, and a failure parameter ζ ∈ (0, 1), a randomized algorithm returns b S ⊆ F with |b S| ≤ h always, cost(b S) ≤ (1 + 2/e + ε)P with probability at least 1 − ζ. Its running time is polynomial in N and log(1/ζ) for the fixed parameters. The algorithm is not given O, P, the partition, or its proxies.
